question: You are one of three finalists. A panel member privately tells you that one of the other two has been rejected. Have your chances improved?
answer: They were always going to be able to name a rejected candidate among the other two, whoever wins — so hearing one name tells you nothing about you. Your one-in-three stands, and the remaining finalist now carries two-thirds.
move: Information only moves the odds if it could have come out differently.
trap: Two candidates left, so it feels like a coin flip.
